other.charge: commercial pure Mg (99.95 wt.%), Zn (99.95 wt.%) and Mg–20 wt.% RY master alloy

evidence.quote: was prepared from commercial pure Mg (99.95 wt.%), Zn (99.95 wt.%) and Mg–20 wt.% RY master alloy in an electric resistant furnace under the protection of a mixed atmosphere of CO2 and SF6.
The alloy melt was homogenized at about 750 ◦C for 0.5 h.
Then it was poured into a water-cooled mould at approximately 720 ◦C.
The ingot was homogenized at 500 ◦C for 12 h.
Then it was extruded at 460 ◦C with an extrusion ratio of about 17.

attributes.morphology: bent long strip along extrusion direction; fine lamellae inside DRX grains

evidence.quote: the extra diffraction spots at the ±1/14(0 0 0 2)/H9251, ±2/14(0 0 0 2)/H9251, ±3/14(0 0 0 2)/H9251. . .. . .±13/14(0 0 0 2)/H9251positions, which is a convincing evidence to prove the existence of 14H LPSO structure

attributes.morphology: block-like at grain boundaries/interdendritic regions and fine lamellae in grain interior
attributes.location: grain boundaries, interdendritic regions, grain interior

evidence.quote: Both of the ﬁne-lamellar phase and the gray block-like phase have a special structure which has been reported as the LPSO structure.
The small irregular particles marked as A are determined to be the Mg3RY2Zn3 phase because their Zn/RY (in at.%) ratio of 1.48 is close to 1.5.
the cuboid-shaped phase marked as B is Mg24(RY, Zn)5
The average dendritic arm spacing (DAS) of the as-cast alloy is 45 ± 5 /H9262m.

attributes.morphology: fine, randomly oriented around strip-like LPSO phase

evidence.quote: The average size of the DRX gains in the as-extruded alloy is about 8 ± 2 /H9262m which is much smaller than the DAS in the as-cast alloy.

attributes.morphology: straight, uniformly distributed, same orientation within one grain

evidence.quote: The fringes of individual lamellae are uniformly distributed and the spacing between them was measured to be ∼1.8 nm

attributes.location: interfaces between strip-like LPSO phase and α-Mg matrix

evidence.quote: the c + a dislocations piling up at the interfaces between the strip-like LPSO phase and the /H9251-Mg matrix

the existence of the LPSO phase with high volume fraction in alloys plays an important role in enhancing the reﬁnement of Mg recrystallized grains during extrusion according to the particle stimulated nucleation (PSN) mechanism
the grain reﬁnement induced by hot-extrusion and LPSO phase is effective in increasing strength as well as ducility

mechanisms.name: basal slip hindering by LPSO phase

evidence.quote: the formation of LPSO phase increases the critical resolved shear stress (CRSS) of the basal plane so as to hinder the basal slip which is beneﬁcial to the strengthening of the alloys

the visible c + a dislocations as shown in Fig. 6(b) suggest that the LPSO phase is favorable to activation of non-basal slip in the Mg matrix and it can contribute to the improvement of the ductility

mechanisms.name: external stress assisted LPSO nucleation and growth

evidence.quote: the external stress can effectively enhance the nucleation and growth of the LPSO structure during the thermal deformation process
